coverage.evergreenHorizonNote: Evergreen accepts a maximum durationWeek of 28 days, so the ShipmentLink sweep sees 4 weeks (W38-W41), not the full 8-week window. A second pass departing 13 Oct was run from Pusan to New York and returned only 7 rows against 21 for the near window, so Evergreen forward data thins out sharply beyond 4 weeks. Absence of a sailing in W42-W45 on Evergreen is weak evidence, not a clean negative.

serviceAliases._note: EC4 gained AUG this run. On CNYTN-USHOU Evergreen sold three AUG sailings (ONE ARCADIA 079E departing 01 Oct, CONTI CORTESIA 014E departing 16 Sep, EVER LUCKY 085E departing 05 Oct) and ONE returned the same vessels and voyage numbers under EC4 on the same lane (ONE ARCADIA 079E 03 Oct, EVER LUCKY 085E 07 Oct), with the small date difference being cut-off versus sailing. AUG is Evergreen marketing on the Premier Alliance Gulf string, not a separate service and not an extra loader. It stays in the registry so it never raises a NEW SERVICE alert again.

ignoredCodeNotes.MS2: Discharges Los Angeles and moves to Houston by rail. ONE prints it as Direct on CNYTN-USHOU (six sailings at 20 to 24 days this run), which is exactly the trap. Drop at parse time, always.
ignoredCodeNotes.NSB: Evergreen intra-Asia relay. Surfaced four times on KRPUS-USNYC at 39 to 50 days with southbound S voyage suffixes, against 24 to 25 days for the direct strings on the same pair. Transshipment first leg, not a USEC service.
ignoredCodeNotes.KTH: Same pattern as NSB. Five sightings on KRPUS-USNYC at 47 to 50 days with S suffixes.
ignoredCodeNotes.FP2: ONE relay code. Three sightings on CNYTN-USNYC this run, every one flagged Transshipment by ONE itself.

detectorTraps: Hapag isGemini false is context, not a trigger. AA7 returned five times with isGemini false on CNYTN-USNYC and CNYTN-USSAV this run and is a normal Wan Hai / Hapag VSA.
Maersk isRoutingAdhoc is NOT an ad-hoc indicator. Verified 16 Sep 2026 on CNYTN-USHOU: the flag was true on all five routings returned, including four routine TP15 sailings. Never trigger on it.
An ad-hoc code does not imply a fixed rotation. Work up every voyage individually; OGEC has carried at least three unrelated rotations across voyages 0020 and 0021.
Evergreen point-to-point prints the port cut-off in one column and the sailing date in another. Always take the ETD column.

vsProforma.basis: Measured this run on the same pair used last run. Evergreen CNNGB-USNYC returned five NUE2 sailings at 21, 30, 30, 30 and 30 days (median 30). OGEC sails Ningbo 20 Sep and arrives New York 16 Oct, 26 days. Last run the same comparison came out at zero delta; the gap opened because the Ningbo departure moved five days later while the New York arrival did not move at all, so the voyage is now scheduled to make the time up at sea. Treat -4 as a schedule artefact of the slip, not as a genuinely faster string.

Shanghai departure 13 Sep became 16 Sep, Ningbo 15 Sep became 20 Sep, Pusan 17 Sep became 22 Sep, Panama Canal departure 6 Oct became 10 Oct and Boston arrival 25 Oct became 26 Oct. New York (16 Oct), Savannah (21 Oct) and Baltimore (28 Oct) arrivals are unchanged. items.note: Unchanged this run. Every ETA and ETD matches the 14 Sep record exactly. All five Asia departures are in window: Port Klang 30 Sep (W40), Cai Mep 05 Oct (W41), Shekou 11 Oct (W41), Ningbo 15 Oct (W42) and Qingdao 19 Oct (W43). The AA9 CSV now carries a second vessel, WAN HAI 712 on voyage E002 as well, with Port Klang 23 Aug, Shekou 30 Aug, Ningbo 03 Sep and Qingdao 06 Sep. Every one of those departures is before the window opens, so it is not published as an item, and its US legs are internally inconsistent (New York arrival 24 Oct printed ahead of Norfolk 22 Oct), which is why it was already moved to history rather than carried. Standing classification caveat: two voyages under one code, both numbered E002, is starting to look less like a pure one-off and more like a thin string Wan Hai is running opportunistically. If a third AA9 voyage appears with an in-window departure, reclassify AA9 as a service and move it to the registry.

items.note: Unchanged this run and now confirmed from two independent Maersk surfaces. The vessel schedule gives Gwangyang 19 Sep, Yantian 22-23 Sep, Busan 27-28 Sep and Panama Canal 21 Oct; the point-to-point search gives the Houston arrival of 31 Oct at Barbours Cut with a 38 day 10 hour transit. The vessel schedule stops at the canal and does not print the Houston call, which is why both surfaces are needed. Caution flag recorded this run: the routing-unified response carries a boolean isRoutingAdhoc and it is true on all five routings returned for this lane, including the four ordinary TP15 sailings. It is not an ad-hoc indicator and must never be used as a trigger. This item rests on the service code alone: XL is not in the registry, it returned once against TP15 four times on the same lane, and the vessel leaves the Pacific after Houston rather than turning back to Asia.

alerts.message: Blocked last run, working this run. The point-to-point UI search completed normally and the routing-unified replay returned HTTP 200 with five routings. This is what let XL-MAERSK-MONTANA-639E be re-verified from two surfaces instead of carried on trust. Recipe that worked: one real UI search on maersk.com/schedules/pointToPoint with the fetch wrapper installed first, then replay the captured POST with cargo forced to DRY and no credentials include.

Hapag CNYTN-USNYC returned AA7 5 with isGemini false and US4 6 with isGemini true, and nothing was flagged, exactly as the regression fixture requires. Evergreen CNSHA-USNYC returned NUE2 4, SAX 4, CBX 3, NUE 3, OGEC 1 and flagged OGEC only. Evergreen CNYTN-USNYC returned SAX 3, AUE 3, CBX 4 with no OGEC and flagged nothing.

No first sighting this run. All three published items reappeared with full rotations. Every non-registry code encountered resolved to something other than an extra loader: AUG to EC4 by matching vessel and voyage, FP2 and MS2 to relay or rail routings, NSB and KTH to Evergreen intra-Asia feeder legs.

Lanes not covered this run: evergreen CNSHA-USHOU, evergreen CNNGB-USSAV, evergreen CNNGB-USHOU, evergreen VNTOT-USSAV, evergreen VNTOT-USHOU, evergreen KRPUS-USSAV, evergreen KRPUS-USHOU, hapag CNSHA-USSAV, hapag CNSHA-USHOU, hapag CNNGB-USSAV, hapag CNNGB-USHOU, hapag KRPUS-USSAV, hapag KRPUS-USHOU, maersk all lanes except CNYTN-USHOU, msc all lanes except CNYTN-USNYC, one all lanes except CNYTN-USNYC and CNYTN-USHOU, all CMA CGM lanes. CMA CGM was not attempted at all, by design, because its DataDome quota is shared with the liner-tracker-market-refresh task on the same IP. Hapag returned zero routes for Cai Mep to New York under both VNCMT and VNTOT, so that lane is uncovered on Hapag rather than empty. Evergreen coverage is 4 weeks, not 8; see coverage.evergreenHorizonNote.

OGEC voyages 0020 and 0021 were consecutive, roughly a week apart, which is why this is treated as a rolling ad-hoc programme rather than a one-off. No voyage 0022 appeared on any Evergreen lane this run, including the second pass departing 13 Oct from Pusan. Evergreen forward visibility is thin past 4 weeks, so this is not yet evidence the programme has stopped. Check for 0022 again next run; if it is still absent with an in-window departure date two runs running, downgrade the rolling-programme assumption.

AA9 now has two published voyages, WAN HAI 903 E002 in window and WAN HAI 712 E002 out of window, both under the same voyage number. A third voyage would make AA9 a service rather than an extra loader. Decide next run.
